audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 phase why described Noxian Guillotine turning 5-stack trades into kills, which is a Darius-favoured line sitting under a phase whose side is Aurora and whose rating is 3/10. The stage that actually flips at 6 is hers, and Between Worlds' numbers were never given.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140/120/100 seconds and 250 range: 'Aurora leaps in a direction of her choosing, releasing a shockwave that damages and slows any enemies it hits. Afterward, she creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other.' Noxian Guillotine is 460 range, so a teleport across her own zone is enough to break the lock even though the ultimate is off cooldown.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds lands at 6: a shockwave slow and a zone she teleports across, so your 460-range Guillotine loses the target.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two separate fabrications ran through this matchup. (a) The whole full layer tracks an ability called 'Twofold Hunt', sometimes annotated '(Blink)'. No such ability exists: Aurora's Q is Twofold Hex, a 900-range curse missile with a recast, and it is not a blink. (b) Five content fields call Across the Veil an 'untargetable' dash and The Weirding a 'root'. Riot's text gives Across the Veil invisibility, not untargetability, and gives The Weirding a slow plus a backward hop, with no root anywhere in the kit.
audit.why: Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s, 700 range): 'Aurora leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible, and gaining Move Speed.' The Weirding (E, 15/14/13/12/11s, 825 range): 'sends out a blast of spirit magic that damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward to safety.' The distinction matters for play: invisibility breaks Noxian Guillotine's target lock the same way untargetability would, but Hemorrhage is already applied and keeps ticking through it, so a trade banked to 3+ stacks is not undone by her W. The decisive cooldown gap is Apprehend at 26s rank 1 against Across the Veil at 22s - she has her leap back before your pull at rank 1, and that gap closes to 16s vs 18s by rank 5, which is when the lane turns.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil is a 22s leap that ends in invisibility, not untargetability; The Weirding slows and hops her back, it never roots you.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named the tracked cooldown as 'Twofold Hunt' and gave no numbers for it, for Apprehend, or for Noxian Guillotine.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16 - the longest non-ultimate cooldown in either kit. Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18. Noxian Guillotine is 120/100/80 and its cooldown is refreshed on a killing blow.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil 22s, Apprehend 26s at rank 1 falling to 16s, Noxian Guillotine 120s at rank 1 and refunded on a kill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Aurora as 'he' and 'his' in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, breakdown.mid and dontsFull[0].d.
audit.why: Aurora is female; Riot's own ability text uses 'she' and 'her' throughout. A page that misgenders the enemy reads as machine-generated and undermines the rest of the advice.

The two claims reconcile once the stage is framed as the side lane: at two items Stridebreaker runs a squishy mage down, while her scaling shows up in grouped fights, which is what the late paragraph is about.

notes: The fabricated ability 'Twofold Hunt' is not confined to this matchup - it is the tracked-cooldown token for every Aurora field in champ-data/darius.full.js and it is annotated '(Blink)' in several. I corrected the instances I could fit; breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, winCon, loading, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d and report[12..13].t all still carry it. Aurora's W is invisibility, not untargetability - I did NOT assert whether a control ward or Oracle Lens reveals it, because that is not in Riot's text. Same for whether Noxian Guillotine can be buffered onto her during the leap. The kit file flags Apprehend as 'knockup'; Riot's description says only that it pulls enemies to him, with no knockup and no slow, so I never wrote either - that derived flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire and it will mislead any agent that trusts it.
